units.text: Christ School took the boys basketball 4A titles Carmel lost in 2023 (48–53) and 2025 (50–73, as Christ School three-peated), and Cannon took the 2021 final (85–94); Rabun Gap-Nacoochee beat Carmel in the 2021 (1–0) and 2022 (1–0) boys soccer 4A finals, and Coastal Christian in the 2019 3A final; Providence Day shut Carmel out for the 2026 girls soccer 4A title (0–2).
Built from the school’s own "Next Steps" list of college signees and its signing-day posts; division and conference labels were added by the researcher from each college’s NCAA or NAIA status.

Four of the six Division I commits are basketball players who signed with mid-major programs in the Big South, Sun Belt and Southern conferences; the other two are tennis players, one of them Carmel’s Power 4 signee, Gabe Avram (’24), at South Carolina in the SEC. Kam Taylor reached the ACC (Florida State) only later, through the transfer portal, not as a Carmel commit.

Most Carmel signees land in NCAA Division II and III: baseball to Lander, USC Aiken, Bluefield State and Ferrum; basketball to Fayetteville State and Johnson & Wales, and to WVU Tech in the NAIA; golf to North Greenville and Randolph-Macon; volleyball to Winston-Salem State. Tennis is the program’s second pipeline — six signees in the classes of 2024 and 2025, from the SEC to Johns Hopkins. The school’s list also includes a dance-team signee, who is not counted here as an athletic commitment.

Cade Tyson (’22) was 2022 NC Mr. Basketball and left as the program’s recruiting headliner (Belmont → UNC → Minnesota; a 2026 NBA G League Draft Combine / Portsmouth invitee). Jaeden Mustaf, all-state at Carmel and son of ex-NBA Jerrod Mustaf, led the 2022–23 team to 28–4 and the state final before Georgia Tech → Indiana. Cody Peck (6'10", four-star, top-100 → Dayton) is often linked to Carmel but played only two seasons there and graduated elsewhere — he is not a Carmel commit.

Every row is from the school’s own "Next Steps" signee list or its signing-day and news posts; level labels (P4 / D1 / D2 / D3 / NAIA) and conferences were added by the researcher from each college’s status. P4 = SEC · Big Ten · ACC · Big 12. The Class of 2026 rows are the signees the school has announced so far; its list for that class is not yet published.

Cade Tyson (’22) — 2022 North Carolina Mr. Basketball, averaging 24.0 ppg as a senior and scoring 31 in the state-title win over Greensboro Day. Belmont → UNC → Minnesota; a 2026 NBA G League Draft Combine and Portsmouth invitee (a draft prospect, not yet a pro).

Carmel’s athletics pages reference a coaches directory but list no head-coach names, tenures or career records. Those details are unpublished on the pages fetched — a deeper pass (school directory, press) would be needed to populate a coaching ledger.

Class of 2025 basketball alumnus Bryce Slay signed his first NIL deal — with College HUNKS (College Hunks Hauling Junk & Moving) — described as among the first Charlotte high-school graduates to secure such an agreement. No dollar figure was disclosed; the deal was initiated by his parents, Tamar (ex-Charlotte Bobcats) and Celeste Slay. Slay had committed to Marshall.

Levels shown are what the sources actually publish. Volleyball is the one sport whose ladder is documented — MaxPreps lists varsity, JV and freshman teams — so it is the only row carrying a JV chip; every other sport shows V alone because the athletics site that would list its ladder is JavaScript-rendered and exposes nothing to a fetch. The Middle School fields its own teams in soccer, basketball, track & field and swimming (grades 6–8, subject to academic standing and behavior), but the school does not publish a full MS roster, so no MS chips are claimed. Cheering and track & field come from Private School Review rather than the MaxPreps season grid.

every other program. The 14 titles since 2021 sit in six sports — girls tennis, volleyball, boys soccer, boys golf, boys track and girls swimming — and the school publishes no championship history of its own, so this ledger rests on association results and local coverage.

The most decorated program at the school: NCISAA 2A champions in 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025. The 2024 win over Epiphany School was described in coverage as the program’s third state championship in four years and fourth overall; the 2025 win over the same opponent made it three straight.

Won the NCISAA 2A title in 2021, 2022 and 2024, and lost the 2025 final 1–4 to Caldwell Academy. The 2024 win was a shutout of Westchester Country Day, completing a three-title school year alongside volleyball and girls tennis — the run local coverage headlined as "Déjà vu".

Both Division I commits are volleyball players: Megan Brown (’24) at Wofford in the Southern Conference, and Anne Bradley Bing (’25) at South Carolina in the SEC — Gaston Day’s one Power 4 commitment in this window.

Volleyball, Gaston Day’s state-championship program, produced both Division I commits; Braylen Todd (’26) went on to play basketball at Johnson & Wales in Charlotte. The school publishes no signing list or signing-day announcements, so the count is a documented minimum. Bree Smith (’27), a 50 and 100 freestyle swimmer, has committed to swim at Stanford.

Each row is the college the athlete went to out of Gaston Day, as listed on that college’s own roster. P4 = SEC · Big Ten · ACC · Big 12. Johnson & Wales in Charlotte competes in the USCAA rather than the NCAA, so Braylen Todd is listed at the D3 tier for want of a USCAA level in this table’s scale. The Class of 2027 row is a public commitment, listed because it is already announced; it is not counted in the funnel, the sport bars or on the Compare page until the athlete signs.

The athletics page states "30 teams participating in 12 different sports" (Wikipedia says 14 sports / 28 teams). Tennis (boys & girls), Wrestling and Field Hockey appear in MaxPreps' sport inventory but list no head coach on the school's Coaches & Teams page, so a level chip is not drawn for them. Athletic Director Jim Rhodes; Assistant AD Crystal Rhodes.

Three of the four Division I commits are baseball players — Conner Barozzino (’24) at Appalachian State in the Sun Belt, and Davis Cabbage and Ben Green (’25) at UNC Wilmington and UNC Asheville. The fourth is a football player, Jahzir Dukes (’24), a defensive back at North Carolina Central in the MEAC. There are no Power 4 commits in this window.

Baseball — the program behind two of HGCS’s recent state titles — accounts for six of the seven commits, reaching Division II at Wingate and Mars Hill and junior college at Gaston College as well as Division I. The school publishes no all-sport signing list, so the count is a documented minimum.

The Coaches & Teams page names a head coach for nearly every varsity, JV and Middle School squad (Cross Country and Golf coaches Elizabeth Hamilton, Keith White and Todd Staples; Swimming Sam Cox; Cheer Carmen Costner among them), but publishes no bios, career records or tenure lengths — so no pedigree or continuity claim can be made from public sources.

Selected results, not a record — Trinity has published exactly two seasons, Fall 2023 and Winter 2024, all of it Queen City Conference play. WINTER 2024: "For the first time in school history, the Trinity 8th Grade boys' basketball team won the Queen City Conference championship on Feb. 8 to cap their undefeated season." The title was clinched in a 54–23 win at home over Carmel Christian. FALL 2023: the girls cross country team was "conference champion for the 4th year running, ranked first among independent schools in North Carolina, and had 7 runners named all-conference." Alongside it, the 7th/8th Grade boys soccer team won both the conference title and the tournament championship; the 8th Grade volleyball team tied for first; and boys cross country placed third, with 3 runners in the top 15 and 1 named all-conference.

Martin has helmed the basketball team since its beginning in 2004 when he joined Trinity. By his count, some 250 students have played on the 8th Grade team in that time — the school's own hedge, and it should be carried rather than presented as a counted figure. There had been many close brushes with a championship before the Feb. 8, 2024 win: "For 20 daggum years, I have thought about this moment pretty much nonstop," Martin said. "I can't explain how much energy has gone into trying to win this tournament championship over the last 20 years." He is Athletic Director as well as head coach, which is what a K–8 athletics department of this size looks like from the inside.
